message.subject: Going down to one product
message.body:
Hello,

I'd like to go down to one product from my next billing date on 3 October, please. I'll keep the oil and drop the capsules, purely to keep costs down.

Could you let me know what my new monthly amount will be? I'm on the concession price at the moment.

Many thanks,
Nadia Kaur

policy.label: Policy P5.4: Prices, price changes and concessions
policy.text:
Monthly plan prices. United Kingdom: one product £112, two products £164; concession £90 and £131.

Price changes. We give at least 30 days' notice by email. A new price applies from the first billing date on or after the date it takes effect.

Concessions. About 20% off for holders of an Australian Pensioner Concession Card or Health Care Card, a New Zealand Community Services Card, or, in the UK, proof of a means-tested benefit such as Universal Credit. A concession is verified when it is added and re-verified every 12 months; we email a reminder 30 days before it is due. If it is not re-verified in time, the standard price applies from the next billing date, and the concession price returns from the next billing date after it is verified again. Patients re-verify by uploading their card or letter under Billing in their account. A new concession is added the same way, and the concession price applies from the next billing date after it is verified.

A change to the products on a plan changes the price from the next billing date. There is no referral programme and there are no discount codes.

policy.label: Policy P6.1: Pausing, cancelling or changing a plan
policy.text:
Pausing. A plan can be paused for 1 to 3 months at a time. Ask at least 3 days before the next billing date for the pause to apply to that order. With less notice, we can still stop the order and refund it if it has not been dispensed. A paused plan can restart early at any time: the first order goes out on the restart date, which becomes the new billing date. Plans are monthly; there is no two-monthly option, but a pause can space orders out.

Cancelling. A plan can be cancelled at any time with no fee. With at least 3 days' notice before the billing date there are no further charges. Orders that have already been dispatched cannot be recalled.

Changing products. Adding, removing or swapping a product needs a clinician's approval. Once approved, the change and any new price apply from the next billing date.

Stop sending. If a patient says to stop sending, stop, or not send anything more, put every order that has not been dispatched on hold straight away, before replying. Then ask whether they want to pause or cancel. The hold stays until the patient confirms. Reply within 1 business day. If the reason is a health concern, the message goes to a clinician (see clinical questions).

policy.label: Policy P5.1: Plan charges, billing dates and receipts
policy.text:
A monthly plan is charged on its billing date, which is the same day each month as the day the plan started, in the patient's local currency. The charge covers the prescribed products for that month, standard delivery and follow-up consults.

A receipt is emailed after every charge. Patients can download copies from Billing in their account, and support can resend any receipt or add the patient's address to it.

A card check (pre-authorisation) can appear as a pending amount for up to 5 business days before it drops off. It is not a second charge.

Patients can move their billing date once every 3 months. The first charge on the new date covers the days in between, pro rata. Patients update their card in their account under Billing; support never takes card numbers by chat or email.
